outside.waitsOn: this module: code the checker accepts under the standard's settings
tests: R5 R31 each outside scanner answers one verdict per engine it reports, found or clean, each engine in its family
R5 R13 the request carries the bytes and required parameters only: no file name, address, member, callback or metadata
R5 not_scanned: TOO_LARGE (nothing sent), SERVICE_REFUSED with the status, SERVICE_UNREACHABLE, TIME_LIMIT
R5 R2 a derived target (area "derived") is read from ${store}/derived/<sha>, checked as a capture is, and sent; any other area is BAD_TARGET, nothing sent
R5 an outside tool's address carrying a user name or password is refused TOOL_ADDRESS_HAS_CREDENTIAL and nothing is sent
R22 private mode per call: confirmed, refused before anything is sent, contradicted by the vendor's answer
R23 a sandbox: submitted, running, then one verdict per engine (found, suspicious, clean); TIME_LIMIT past SANDBOX_TIMEOUT_MS
R24 a safe view by a rebuilding tool: the rebuilt file with its digest, origin, type, what was removed and the tool; CDR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE; nothing stored
R25 reputation: Cloudflare's lookup in the group's account; Web Risk by hash prefix only, never the address
R26 a refresh writes the list under reputation/<tool_id>/, replacing the last only once complete and its checksum holds
R27 a counts record goes in each sink's transport shape and nothing else is added
R27 any other key, a string, a negative or a fraction is COUNTS_RECORD_INVALID, naming the key, and nothing is sent
R28 every catalogued tool's test probe passes through its own adapter; a failing one says what failed; no capture is read
R30 ICAP: RESPMOD over TCP or TLS; 204 or a bare 200 clean; X-Infection-Found or X-Virus-ID found; any other status unknown
R30 azure_blob: written to the organization's container, its index tag read, the blob deleted after
R12 every outside call reaches only its descriptor's hosts for the spec's region, or the spec's own host
R13 sentinel credentials appear in no answer, log line, bucket object or address, across every adapter
R17 each catalogued adapter runs against its vendor's stub, which asserts no file name, member or address is sent
R19 validateDescriptor: ok for a whole descriptor; DESCRIPTOR_MALFORMED naming the field; pure, never throws
R19 the refusals, in order: shares samples, handling not stated, never_sends incomplete, address would leave, private mode unverifiable
R20 the catalogue: exactly the offered descriptors by kind, each passing R19 with its source and date; refused and held by name; frozen
R20 a generic template is completed by the administrator's statement and the spec's host, and R19 validates the result
R21 the spec's checks answer 400 by name and send nothing: unknown, refused (with its reason), held, kind, credentials, handling, reach
R17 every REFUSED_PROVIDERS and HELD_PROVIDERS id is refused by name on every route
R29 GET /providers answers the offered descriptors whole, the refused, the held and the generic transports; no credential value
R19 each descriptor and generic template states config [{name, label, required, structured?}], each name once; a malformed list is DESCRIPTOR_MALFORMED config
R21 the spec's config: each required field present, else CONFIG_MISSING naming it and nothing sent; a field the list does not name is never sent
R29 GET /providers answers each descriptor's and each generic template's config list
R31 engine families: clamav's is ["clamav"]; differentEngine is true exactly when two families share no name
R19 every generic template and every descriptor needing an address hosts does not give lists host, labelled and required (region where it applies)
R19 a config entry whose value is not one text says so: a template's engine_family and source_urls structured "list", its handling structured "handling"; every other entry one text
R19 R21 host and region in a config list are the spec's own fields: read from the spec, checked as R21 says, never sent inside config
R26 reputationRefresh gives the real failed refresh answer: a bad checksum names its threat list, an unreadable list names LIST_UNREADABLE, both keep the last good list
R32 every text GET /providers, /version, the refusals and the test probes answer holds none of the three refused terms
R32 control: a served string holding a refused term is caught; an interface key is not
R32 what a rebuilding tool gives is a "safe view" in the test probe's words
R32 the interface is unchanged: the kind token cdr, LOG_COUNT_KINDS' safe_copies, the codes and field names
